scope: High-priority claim-level evidence for ethylene, defense signaling, micronutrient interpretation, bacterial disease, and virus/viroid differential-diagnosis lessons.
rules: Mappings remain review-pending and do not authorize publication.
Direct cannabis/hemp evidence is bounded to the studied genotype, treatment, pathogen, and method.
General nutrient or defense interpretation must not be converted into universal cannabis thresholds.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis sex expression can be altered experimentally by chemical interventions affecting hormone pathways, supporting a role for hormone signaling while not reducing sex determination to a single hormone.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Garcia-de Heer, Kretzschmar, and Mieog 2026, Plants 15(9):1291, DOI 10.3390/plants15091291.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's cannabis-specific statement that ethylene-related signaling can participate in sex-expression manipulation.
claimEvidence.limitations: Treatment effects are chemical-, dose-, stage-, genotype-, and protocol-specific and do not establish universal cultivation use or legal suitability.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Salicylic-acid and other hormone signals can alter cannabis prenyltransferase promoter activity and cannabinoid-pathway responses, demonstrating signaling-pathway effects without proving crop-wide disease resistance or yield benefit.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Sands et al. 2023, Scientific Reports 13:8620, DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-35303-4.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's cannabis-specific mechanistic example linking defense-related hormone signaling and cannabinoid-pathway regulation.
claimEvidence.limitations: Promoter and metabolite responses do not establish universal elicitor prescriptions, disease efficacy, residue safety, or productivity gains.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Hemp and drug-type Cannabis can differ in nutrient acquisition, utilization, phenology, and source-sink relationships, so nutrient interpretation should preserve genotype and production-type context rather than assume one universal crop response.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Wee et al. 2025, Journal of Experimental Botany 76(1):94-108, DOI 10.1093/jxb/erae362.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports cannabis-specific nutrient-use and source-sink context used alongside general plant micronutrient physiology.
claimEvidence.limitations: The review emphasizes nitrogen and phosphorus and does not establish validated cannabis deficiency/toxicity thresholds for Mn, Zn, Cu, or Mo.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Serratia marcescens has been demonstrated to cause a leaf-spot disease on industrial hemp, providing a confirmed bacterial Cannabis pathosystem while leaving many other bacterial detections non-causal until pathogenicity evidence exists.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Schappe, Ritchie, and Thiessen 2020, Plant Disease 104(4):1248, DOI 10.1094/PDIS-04-19-0782-PDN.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's distinction between confirmed bacterial disease and opportunistic/endophytic detection.
claimEvidence.limitations: One confirmed pathosystem does not make bacterial disease the default explanation for angular, necrotic, or water-soaked lesions.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis/hemp can host multiple viruses and viroids, and molecular detection must be separated from causal attribution of nonspecific mosaic, chlorosis, curling, or stunting symptoms; BCTV is one confirmed hemp virus with genotype- and context-dependent effects.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Punja et al. 2024, IJMS 25(1):14, DOI 10.3390/ijms25010014; Han et al. 2026, Phytopathology 116(5):813-824, DOI 10.1094/PHYTO-09-25-0297-R.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's symptom-overlap, molecular-diagnostics, and causal-inference boundaries for virus/viroid-like presentations.
claimEvidence.limitations: Detection does not establish symptom causation for every sample, and BCTV findings should not be generalized to all viruses, cultivars, regions, or coinfections.
